title: A Reproducible Synthetic Benchmark and Deterministic Validator for Evaluating LLM‑Driven NetOps: A Paired Confirmatory Comparison of a GVR Pipeline and Single‑Pass Generation
abstract: We preregistered, executed, and archived a sealed, machine‑checkable synthetic benchmark and deterministic validator to compare a generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline against a frozen single‑pass LLM on operational intent→configuration tasks. The confirmatory paired design used N=300 tasks (four intent clusters, 75 each) and the declared model gpt-5-mini; validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (v5.0). The orchestration used a shared‑initial candidate per task (both conditions reuse the same initial generation) and allowed at most one automated repair call per failed candidate. Execution accounting: planned_episode_count = 600, completed_episode_count = 600, model_calls_used = 301 (300 shared initial calls + 1 repair); execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 0d841d29dd190ebe50a1973b0eabfd8801bf81476d395b417145fb5201a5511d. Results: baseline 299/300 passes (0.9967), guarded 300/300 passes (1.0); paired contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference = 0.0033333333333332993; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The preregistered target effect (0.10, ≈80% power) was not observed because the shared initial generator produced a near‑ceiling baseline and the guarded repair stage executed exactly once. We explain the arithmetic ceiling effect, explicitly identify how auditors can locate the single repair provider trace (the unique record with stage="repair" in execution/raw_results.jsonl, SHA‑256 above), disclose which preregistered secondary estimands were not produced by the analysis artifacts, and archive all artifacts to enable stronger future confirmatory tests.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are widely proposed for network operations (NetOps) tasks such as intent→configuration translation, change planning, and automated remediation. Empirical reports show LLMs can draft configuration fragments but often produce syntax, topology, or semantic errors; consequently, generate–validate–repair (GVR) and tool‑assisted prompting architectures that combine LLM generation with deterministic verification and targeted repair have been proposed to reduce misconfiguration risk. However, the community lacks standardized, machine‑checkable benchmarks that pair explicit intent tasks with deterministic validator semantics and sealed preregistration for confirmatory comparisons. We therefore preregistered and executed study ac-2026-003-prereg-v1 to (1) build a deterministic synthetic intent→configuration task bank, (2) provide a snapshot deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) that enforces ordering and workflow policies, and (3) run a paired confirmatory comparison of a guarded GVR pipeline versus a frozen single‑pass generator under a constrained repair budget. Our preregistered research question was: under fixed seeds and at most one repair call per failed candidate, does GVR materially increase per‑task validator pass rate relative to a frozen single‑pass LLM?
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and reviews document an accelerating literature applying LLMs to network management and emphasize core challenges—hallucination, prompt injection, and the need for verification—that limit operational deployment [https://openalex.org/W4406137434, https://openalex.org/W4415071524, https://openalex.org/W4402742293]. Empirical work demonstrates that out‑of‑the‑box LLMs can synthesize router configurations but often require verifier assistance or human adjudication to reach operational correctness [https://openalex.org/W4388629193, 10.1145/3626111.3628194]. Prototype GVR and tool‑assisted prompting approaches can improve final correctness in focused datasets [https://openalex.org/W4404652946], but existing demonstrations are dataset‑specific and limited in scale. Security and prompt‑injection analyses motivate guarded architectures and deterministic validators as operational safeguards [https://openalex.org/W4405181600, https://openalex.org/W4388886073]. Our study contributes a sealed, archived, machine‑checkable proof‑of‑concept benchmark and a preregistered paired run that links a deterministic validator to an automated repair trigger under a tightly specified retry and budget policy.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary hypothesis. We froze the confirmatory design in preregistration ac-2026-003-prereg-v1 (SHA‑256 = a05938dad3a61e1f4aae518bcb42244009b0403a18387ceeff4be1d86ce87765). Primary hypothesis H1 asserted the GVR pipeline would yield a higher per‑task validator pass rate than the frozen single‑pass generator on N=300 paired tasks (two‑sided α=0.05). The preregistration fixed task generation, validator semantics, inclusion/exclusion rules, missingness handling, repair budget (≤1 repair call per failed candidate), and the analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). All design artifacts are archived.

Task bank and validator. A deterministic task generator produced 300 synthetic tasks partitioned into four intent clusters (reachability, isolation, ACLs, route policies; 75 each). Each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, allowed_fields, workflow_policies, a difficulty label, and a required_sequence that a valid candidate must satisfy. The validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (v5.0) implements full_intent_constraint_validation: it parses candidates into canonical field operations, enforces required_sequence and group/workflow constraints, computes implied final_state, and returns a binary pass/fail with diagnostic traces. Per‑task scoring JSONs record normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, validation_before/after, and the boolean valid flag; these per‑task artifacts are archived under execution/scoring/*.json.

Shared‑initial paired design and repair policy. To isolate the repair contribution we used a shared‑initial design: each task had a single initial generation (shared_initial) that served both as the baseline single‑pass output and as the GVR pipeline’s starting candidate. The guarded GVR condition validated that candidate and, if the validator failed, could invoke up to one automated repair call (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). This design and the exact repair trigger were fixed in the preregistration and recorded in execution/transformation_manifest.json. The declared model was gpt-5-mini and invocation settings are archived in execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820).

Reproducible lookup of the single repair trace. Execution accounting shows the guarded repair stage executed exactly once (provider stage_counts: repair = 1). The authoritative provider call container is execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 0d841d29dd190ebe50a1973b0eabfd8801bf81476d395b417145fb5201a5511d). Auditors can deterministically retrieve the single repair provider trace by filtering execution/raw_results.jsonl for the unique record where stage == "repair"; that record contains the repair provider trace and the pair_id for the discordant episode. Providing the raw_results.jsonl SHA and the explicit filter criterion (stage == "repair") allows deterministic lookup without reproducing hosted provider outputs. The execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json cross‑reference these entries for verifier convenience.

Preregistered analyses and omitted secondary estimands. The primary estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline with an exact McNemar two‑sided inferential test and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Preregistered secondary estimands included per_task_failure_rate_guarded, per_task_failure_rate_baseline, and effect_size_Cohen_h_equivalent_for_paired_proportions. The analysis artifacts archived with the run contain the confirmatory executor outputs but no populated secondary_results; consequently the preregistered secondary estimands were not produced as distinct result objects in the archived analysis outputs (see Analysis and Missingness below) and are explicitly disclosed as unpopulated in Results.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and provider audit. The execution manifest records: started_at_utc = 2026-08-29T12:41:43.384097+00:00, completed_at_utc = 2026-08-29T13:07:38.995000+00:00, planned_episode_count = 600, completed_episode_count = 600, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 301, artifact_hash_count = 2108. Provider_call_audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 301, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 301, stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 300, repair: 1}, and condition_counts = {shared: 300, guarded: 1}. These stage_counts document that the guarded repair stage executed exactly once across N=300 tasks.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. Aggregated counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv) show baseline_success_count = 299/300 (baseline_success_rate = 0.9966666666666667) and guarded_success_count = 300/300 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0033333333333332993. The exact McNemar two‑sided p reported by the preregistered executor is 1.0, and the paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.00, 0.01].

Interpretation of the p‑value and the discordant counts. The exact McNemar statistic depends solely on the discordant pair counts (n10, n01). With n10 = 1 and n01 = 0 the two‑sided exact p computed by the preregistered executor equals 1.0; this p‑value reflects the extremely small number of discordant pairs and does not imply strong evidence of no practical effect. Put differently, the observed p‑value arises arithmetically from the contingency margins; the paired bootstrap CI (reported above) provides a more informative depiction of practical uncertainty in this ceiling regime. We therefore present both the exact test and the bootstrap CI to avoid misinterpretation.

Secondary estimand status and missingness. The preregistered secondary estimands (per_task_failure_rate_guarded, per_task_failure_rate_baseline, effect_size_Cohen_h_equivalent_for_paired_proportions) were not emitted as populated artifacts in the archived analysis bundle (analysis/secondary_results empty). The principal reason is that the run produced no failed guarded episodes (guarded failures = 0) and only a single discordant episode (n10 = 1), leaving the preregistered secondary computations uninformative or numerically degenerate; we therefore explicitly report these secondary estimands as unpopulated in the archived analysis and discuss their absence as a limitation below.

Representative task traces. Representative per‑task scoring JSONs archived under execution/scoring/ (examples for tasks 000001–000006 included in the bundle) show normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, validation_before/after, difficulty labels, and validator.valid flags. These illustrate the validator’s enforcement of required_sequence constraints (patterns such as shutdown_configure_restore; make_before_break_uplink_switchover; paired_link_atomic_mtu_change). The unique repair provider trace and the corresponding discordant episode identifier are available as the single entry with stage == "repair" inside execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 given above); auditors may extract that entry to inspect the exact provider trace and pair_id.
sections.discussion:
Why the preregistered hypothesis was not supported. The preregistered target effect (absolute paired gain 0.10 at ≈80% power with N=300) assumed a baseline failure rate sufficiently large to produce discordance under the planned paired analysis. The observed baseline ≈0.9967 makes the preregistered target effect arithmetically unattainable: with these marginals the maximum possible paired gain equals 1/300 ≈ 0.00333 (the observed difference). In addition, the guarded repair stage executed only once (repair = 1), so the guarded condition seldom differed from baseline. These execution facts—near‑ceiling baseline and near‑inert repair engagement—explain the null confirmatory outcome despite correct execution and analysis.

Practical implications. The result quantifies an operational lesson: when generator quality under deterministic sampling is already near ceiling and repair budgets are tightly constrained, localized repair yields negligible marginal benefit. Conversely, in environments with lower generator reliability, adversarial inputs, or relaxed repair policies (iterative repairs, multi‑generation selection), GVR pipelines are more likely to provide measurable operational value. The public artifact bundle enables repeatable evaluation of these harder regimes by (for example) increasing task difficulty, enabling iterative repair budgets, or permitting multiple independent initial generations per task.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the shared‑initial design controls generator variance but does not assess multi‑sample selection or independent guarded sampling strategies; the very small number of discordant pairs reduces statistical resolution. Construct validity: the validator enforces snapshot intent constraints but omits vendor CLI idiosyncrasies and temporal in‑flight behaviors; some operational failure modes may not be captured. External validity: tasks are synthetic (device counts 3–50, abstracted multi‑vendor) and only gpt-5-mini and one validator version were evaluated; results do not generalize to production networks or other models without additional experiments. Conclusion validity: the ceiling baseline and n10 = 1 leave subgroup and failure‑mode inference underpowered.

Recommendations grounded in archived artifacts. The execution and analysis artifacts directly motivate implementable modifications for future confirmatory runs: (A) increase task difficulty or inject adversarial seeds to raise initial failure rates (the task manifests and scoring traces demonstrate where difficulty labels aggregate), (B) permit iterative repair budgets per failed candidate (the single repair trace shows repair inactivity under current budget), (C) allow multiple independent initial generations per task to test selection/reranking strategies, and (D) adopt stateful/emulation validators that model ordered side effects to expose temporal failure modes. Each recommendation maps to archived evidence and is actionable from the provided bundle.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered, executed, and archived a sealed synthetic NetOps benchmark and deterministic validator and ran a paired confirmatory comparison of a guarded GVR pipeline versus a frozen single‑pass gpt-5-mini generator on N=300 intent→configuration tasks. Both approaches achieved near‑perfect pass rates (baseline 299/300; guarded 300/300). The preregistered hypothesis that the GVR pipeline would yield a large (0.10) paired improvement was not supported; this null result is explained by a ceiling baseline and minimal repair engagement (stage_counts show shared_initial_generation=300, repair=1). We explicitly disclose where auditors can retrieve the single repair provider trace (the unique record with stage == "repair" in execution/raw_results.jsonl, SHA‑256 = 0d841d29dd190ebe50a1973b0eabfd8801bf81476d395b417145fb5201a5511d) and which preregistered secondary estimands were unpopulated by the analysis artifacts. All preregistration, execution, per‑task validator traces, provider traces, and analysis artifacts are archived to enable the community to run stronger confirmatory tests that raise baseline failure rates and permit iterative repair strategies where GVR advantages are more likely to be measurable.

disclosure_statement: This study followed the sealed preregistration ac-2026-003-prereg-v1 (preregistration SHA‑256 = a05938dad3a61e1f4aae518bcb42244009b0403a18387ceeff4be1d86ce87765) archived with the execution bundle. Declared model and generation settings (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820) were: declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"; requested_model = "gpt-5-mini"; provider = "openai_responses"; max_output_tokens = 2000; maximum_attempts_per_call = 1; reasoning_effort = "minimal"; store = false; temperature = null. Orchestration/adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 implemented the shared initial generation (one shared call per task) and the guarded generate–validate–repair pipeline with maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version v5.0) implementing scoring rule "full_intent_constraint_validation"; per‑task scorer outputs and validator traces are archived under execution/scoring/*.json. Preregistered analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1 (exact McNemar and paired bootstrap CI; bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000). Execution accounting (authoritative): planned_episode_count = 600, completed_episode_count = 600, complete_pair_count = 300, model_calls_used = 301 (300 shared initial generation calls + 1 repair call). Provider_call_audit recorded stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 300, repair: 1}. The single repair provider trace and the corresponding discordant episode identifier are archived as the unique record with stage == "repair" inside execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 0d841d29dd190ebe50a1973b0eabfd8801bf81476d395b417145fb5201a5511d); auditors can deterministically extract that record by filtering execution/raw_results.jsonl for stage == "repair" and thereby obtain the exact pair_id and the per‑call provider trace. Initial master prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy: a human Research Director selected the topic family and provided pre‑lock constraints and the initial master prompt; after the autonomy lock the autonomous pipeline performed literature synthesis, study selection, sealed preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revision. No manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces snapshot intent constraints but does not model temporal in‑flight execution dynamics, vendor CLI idiosyncrasies, or asynchronous side effects.

External validity: tasks are synthetic (device counts 3–50, abstracted multi‑vendor models) and may not capture production heterogeneity; findings do not imply equivalent performance on real production networks or private customer data.

Ceiling effect: near‑perfect pass rates (baseline 299/300, guarded 300/300) reduce sensitivity to detect the preregistered target effect (0.10) and therefore constrain confirmatory inference about practical superiority of GVR under broader conditions.
Model and scope limits: only gpt-5-mini was declared and evaluated; findings do not generalize to other model families or sizes without further experiments.

GVR engagement: the guarded repair stage executed only once across N=300 tasks (provider recorded stage_counts: shared_initial_generation=300, repair=1), so the guarded condition rarely differed from baseline; this pipeline inactivity constrains conclusions about repair effectiveness under alternative trigger policies or larger repair budgets.
Failure‑mode analysis: only one discordant outcome occurred (n10=1), leaving exploratory failure clustering and subgroup inference underpowered and inconclusive.

Reproducibility caveat: reproducing identical hosted model outputs may require access to the same hosted model release and provider invocation semantics recorded in execution/model_configuration.json and the per‑call provider traces archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 0d841d29dd190ebe50a1973b0eabfd8801bf81476d395b417145fb5201a5511d).

Preregistered secondary estimands: the preregistered secondary analyses (per_task_failure_rate_guarded, per_task_failure_rate_baseline, effect_size_Cohen_h_equivalent_for_paired_proportions) were not produced as populated artifacts in the archived analysis bundle due to the observed near‑ceiling margins and the absence of multiple discordant outcomes; their omission is explicitly disclosed.
